To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
leader orientations to productivity and people, when complemented by leader encouragement of cooperative relationships, contribute to team effectiveness.
leader values for productivity and people, when complemented by encouraging cooperative goals among members, are positively related to team effectiveness in China.

leader productivity and leader people orientations are positively associated with team effectiveness, and the effect of leader productivity on team effectiveness is mediated by leader encouragement of cooperative goals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics that explain the relationships between leader productivity and people orientations, and team effectiveness.
how leader values and goals can be used to develop effective teams.
the question of whether and how leader orientations can influence team effectiveness in a Chinese context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study provides evidence of the importance of the cooperative goals for team effectiveness in China, and that the cooperative goals are the result of the interplay of the leader's productivity and people values and the team members' cooperative relationships.
leader productivity and leader people orientations are positively related to team effectiveness through their influence on team members to develop cooperative goals.
the productivity and people orientations of leaders can be used as a basis for developing effective teams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leaders can influence team effectiveness by strengthening cooperative relationships and encouraging cooperative goals.
leaders can make their teams more effective by encouraging cooperative goals and relationships among their members.
leaders who are oriented toward people and productivity and who are able to develop cooperative goals among their team members are likely to be effective leaders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leader orientations to productivity and to people can be complemented by encouraging team members to work toward cooperative goals.
leaders who are both people-oriented and productivity-oriented are most likely to develop effective teams.
the leader's productivity and people values are not enough to make teams effective.
